canonical_for: the do-not-build marker vocabulary on the task ready projection
doc: THE PREDICATE, stated so a stranger can re-run it. A ready row's three prose fields (`fields` below, ALL THREE — searching any one undercounts) are concatenated and scanned for every `needle`. `case_sensitive:false` lowercases both sides. The row's class is the FIRST entry of `classes` that any matching needle carries, so `classes` IS the precedence order, strongest first. No match, or no populated field, answers nothing and the card is byte-identical to what it has always been. This file is the ONE copy: api/lib/barkpark/tasks/dispatchability.ex reads it at COMPILE TIME and internal/cli/dispatch_markers.json is a byte copy pinned to it by TestDispatchMarkerSpecMirrorsTheServerCopy.

class_meaning.forbidden: An imperative addressed to a DISPATCHER: this row must not be handed to a builder. Do not claim it, do not commission work against it.
class_meaning.deferred: Buildable in principle, but gated or ordered by something outside the builder's reach (an owner, a wave, a queue position). LOOK before dispatching.

calibration.population: 150 open rows from `bp task ls --status open --limit 150` (content-bearing cards: description 150/150, disposition_reason 70/150, operating_instruction 47/150)
calibration.hand_labelled: Every one of the 5 forbidden hits and the 9 deferred hits was read in context and is a TRUE marker (precision 14/14 on this sample). RECALL IS UNMEASURED and the vocabulary is necessarily incomplete — a marker nobody has phrased yet is invisible here, so the absence of a class is never a licence to dispatch, only the absence of a refusal.
calibration.rejected: A bare case-insensitive `backlog` was MEASURED AND REFUSED: 12 of 150 rows match and most are prose or a row id (`dr-backlog-never-started`, `stw-backlog-catalog-family`, 'the ready backlog'). The shouted spellings below are what survive.
